\chapter{Divergences}\label{chap:divergences}

\section*{At a glance}
\begin{itemize}
\item \lead{Source} \code{doc/DIVERGENCES.md}, rendered by \code{blueprint/scripts/render\_registers.py}; the sections below are the register's own text.
\item \lead{Entries} 31.
\end{itemize}

This register lists every place where the verification code on the \texttt{cl/\allowbreak{}verification} branch (\texttt{proof/}, library \texttt{EraseProof}), or the statements it proves, diverge from the references --- Letouzey, "A New Extraction for Coq" (TYPES 2002), and Sozeau et al., "Correct and Complete Type Checking and Certified Erasure for Coq, in Coq" (J. ACM 2025), including its MetaRocq sources at commit \texttt{4b201296} (branch 9.1). The verification follows these references as closely as the differences between Lean's kernel, as con-leche (\texttt{github.com/\allowbreak{}leanprover/\allowbreak{}con-leche}, commit \texttt{d88e04e9b}) checks it, and Rocq/PCUIC/MetaRocq allow; every place it does not, for any reason, is recorded here. Entries land with the artifact that diverges.

Each entry has an id \texttt{DV-\textless{}n\textgreater{}} and exactly these fields:

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} file and declaration on the \texttt{cl/\allowbreak{}verification} branch that carries the divergence.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} the paper section/figure/theorem and the MetaRocq \texttt{file:identifier} it corresponds to.
\item \textbf{What differs:} the concrete difference between our artifact and the reference artifact.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} the concrete reason the divergence is necessary --- a difference between Lean's kernel and CIC, a gap in what con-leche provides, a scope boundary of the verified fragment, or similar. This field must name a real constraint; "it was simpler" or "we chose to" is not a forcing reason.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} the alternative(s) that would have kept the divergence from existing, and why each was rejected.
\end{itemize}

An entry without a forcing reason is a defect, not a divergence: it must be removed and the statement or definition restated to match the reference instead. Differences of representation alone (a judgment in \texttt{Prop} where MetaRocq's lives in \texttt{Type}, explicit flags, bundled helpers) get no entry.

The ids 1 to 31 are those of the register of the Metalean development of this repository (\#16), which continues the register of the lean4lean experiment; the shipping sources and the ported definitions cite them. Only the ids that this branch or the shipping sources cite appear here. An id whose divergence does not arise against con-leche keeps an entry that says so ("Not applicable on this branch"), so that no citation is left without an entry. The ids from 32 on are new.

\section{\texorpdfstring{Trust base}{Trust base}}\label{reg:trust-base}

What the statements and the checks rely on without proof:

\begin{itemize}
\item Lean's kernel at the pinned toolchain (\texttt{lean-toolchain}), and the axioms \texttt{propext}, \texttt{Classical.choice} and \texttt{Quot.sound}: every declaration of the library stays within them (checks C3 to C5), and its modules are replayed through the kernel (check \texttt{replay}, \texttt{leanchecker}). The replay covers the library's modules \texttt{EraseProof.*} and the shipping code's \texttt{LeanToLambdaBox.*}; the compiled \texttt{.olean} files of con-leche that they import are trusted as built.
\item con-leche at the pinned revision (\texttt{d88e04e9b}, \texttt{lake-manifest.json}, pinned in \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}spec.pin}): its checker, run as a function on the program's records (\leandecl{EraseProof.ConLecheAccepts}, \leandecl{EraseProof.CLTyped}, \leandecl{EraseProof.CLCert}), and its set-theoretic model, which the statements quantify over (\leandecl{EraseProof.Sound}). A \texttt{SetTheory} model is a hypothesis of the statements, never an axiom: con-leche instantiates it only from an inaccessibility hypothesis that this development does not use.
\item The shipping oracle \leandecl{Erasure.Pure.isErasable}, which defines the marks (\leandecl{EraseProof.MarkOf}, DV-32), and the helpers through which the statements are defined. \texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}spec.pin} holds a SHA-256 digest of each statement definition and of every definition of the library, of the shipping code or of con-leche that the statements reach (check C12b). The three functions under verification, \leandecl{Erasure.collectDeps}, \leandecl{Erasure.erasePure} and \leandecl{Erasure.eraseEntry}, are pinned by name only.
\item Lean's compiler and runtime for the shipping code. The theorems are about the logical definitions of the three functions; \texttt{\#erase} runs their compiled code. What \texttt{\#erase} does around \leandecl{Erasure.eraseEntry} (the elaboration of the input and of the \texttt{config} term, the printer that writes the program as an S-expression, the \texttt{.inlinings} file, the \texttt{.mli} signature) is not covered.
\end{itemize}

\section{\texorpdfstring{Entries}{Entries}}\label{reg:entries}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-1}{DV-1}}\label{reg:dv-1}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Spec.lean}: \leandecl{EraseProof.toCL?} (with \leandecl{EraseProof.Level.toCL} and \leandecl{EraseProof.Name.toCL}) reads a Lean \texttt{Expr} as a con-leche \texttt{Expr}, and \leandecl{EraseProof.CLTyped} (hypothesis \texttt{hty} of \leandecl{EraseProof.erase_correct_statement}) asks con-leche's full-grade inference to accept the reading of the input; \leandecl{EraseProof.SrcEval} and \leandecl{EraseProof.Erases} evaluate and erase Lean terms.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} PCUIC's weak call-by-value evaluation \texttt{eval} (\texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICWcbvEval.v:231}; MC \S{}5.6) and the erasure relation \texttt{erases} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}Extract.v:88}; MC \S{}7.3, Fig. 18), both on PCUIC terms, the syntax PCUIC's typing judges; the premise \texttt{welltyped} (\texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICTyping.v:355}) of \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}correct} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ErasureCorrectness.v:51}); Letouzey \S{}3.1 (CIC terms).
\item \textbf{What differs:} the syntax that evaluates and the syntax that is typed differ. con-leche's \texttt{Expr} has no binder names or infos, no metavariables and no metadata; \leandecl{EraseProof.toCL?} drops binder names, binder infos and \texttt{mdata} (every mark is therefore transparent to it), keeps \texttt{let} and projections, and is \texttt{none} on a free variable, a metavariable and a level metavariable, as con-leche reads a stored Lean \texttt{Expr} (CL ConLeche/Frontend/Olean/Spec.lean:162 exprNode). The hypothesis \texttt{hty} is a run of con-leche's inference on that reading at some fuel, in place of \texttt{welltyped \ensuremath{\Sigma} [] t}; there is no typing judgement on Lean terms and no relation between the two syntaxes, only the function \texttt{toCL?}. A projection, a \texttt{let} and a literal are evaluated and erased on the Lean term and read by the same function.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} con-leche has no syntactic typing judgement (its theory is a set model, \leandecl{EraseProof.Sound}, DV-34): the only typing it offers is the run of its checker on its own \texttt{Expr}, so a premise on a Lean term can only go through a reading function. The reading has to be a function, with con-leche's own drops, for a statement to mention it; the eraser consumes Lean \texttt{Expr}s.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} con-leche's frontend \texttt{parseExportD} on an export of the program, which is IO code (outside the hygiene allow list of check C6) and not a function of the program's records; a typing relation on Lean \texttt{Expr}, which no development of this repository provides.
\end{itemize}

\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} MetaRocq's translation of Template terms into PCUIC terms, \texttt{trans} (\texttt{template-pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}TemplateToPCUIC.v:63}; MC \S{}9).
\item \textbf{What differs:} Not applicable on this branch. There is no translation relation between two syntaxes (DV-1): \leandecl{EraseProof.toCL?} reads Nat literals, strings and projections directly, as con-leche's frontend does.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} not applicable: the gap that the id recorded in the lean4lean experiment (no rule for literals and projections in the bridge) does not exist.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} dropping the id, which would leave the citations of the earlier registers without an entry.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-3}{DV-3}}\label{reg:dv-3}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Spec.lean}: \leandecl{EraseProof.DeclsOf?} (with \leandecl{EraseProof.declOf?}, \leandecl{EraseProof.blockOf?} and \leandecl{EraseProof.blockShapeOK}) reads the program's declarations, a newest-first list of Lean \texttt{ConstantInfo}s, as con-leche's input; \leandecl{EraseProof.ViewAgrees}; \leandecl{EraseProof.SubEnv}, and the evaluation environment \leandecl{EraseProof.EvalEnv} (\leandecl{EraseProof.evalEnvOf}), over the dependency closure in the hypothesis \texttt{hev} (DV-41) and in the conclusions of \leandecl{EraseProof.erase_correct_statement} and \leandecl{EraseProof.erasePure_erases_statement}; \leandecl{EraseProof.collectDeps_sub_statement}.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} the well-formed global environment \texttt{wf\_\allowbreak{}ext} (\texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICTyping.v:507}; MC \S{}3.6), whose declarations are a newest-first list searched by \texttt{lookup\_\allowbreak{}env} (\texttt{common/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}Environment.v:483}); MetaRocq's \texttt{erase\_\allowbreak{}correct} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ErasureFunctionProperties.v:657}) evaluates the erased term over the erasure of the dependency closure \texttt{erase\_\allowbreak{}global\_\allowbreak{}deps} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ErasureFunction.v:1602}).
\item \textbf{What differs:} the environment is a list of Lean records, and \texttt{DeclsOf?} turns it into con-leche's declarations only if the records agree with one another as Lean's kernel generates them: names are distinct; no type or value carries a mark key (DV-39); unsafe and partial constants are left out as lean4export leaves them out (CL ConLeche/Frontend/Olean/Reads.lean:18 CKindF.skipped); each inductive block passes the record checks of con-leche's frontend (CL ConLeche/Frontend/ExportC.lean:241 validateIndF: one parameter count, constructor positions, field counts, recursor counts) and the checks of the fields the traversal reads and con-leche does not (each type's \texttt{all} and \texttt{numIndices}, the head of each constructor's result type, \texttt{isRec}, the recursors being exactly the \texttt{T.rec} of the block's members, \leandecl{EraseProof.blockShapeOK}). Con-leche checks the whole program; the source evaluation (DV-41) and the erasure relation of the conclusions (\texttt{EvalEnv}, with the markings of the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} dependencies' bodies) range over the closure the fragment test returns, which is a sub-environment of the program (\leandecl{EraseProof.collectDeps_sub_statement}: the constants it reads come from a type or a value con-leche checked, from a record field \texttt{DeclsOf?} checks, or from a compiled pre-definition, whose constants \texttt{ViewAgrees} puts in the program). \texttt{ViewAgrees} also requires that the compiled pre-definitions the view holds for the program's declarations name only constants of the program.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} the eraser reads Lean records through \leandecl{Erasure.EnvView}, and con-leche checks its own \texttt{Declaration}s without the Lean fields (\texttt{induct}, \texttt{all}, \texttt{cidx}, \texttt{isRec}, the recursor list) that the traversal reads: a record con-leche accepts may still disagree with another record the traversal reads, so the agreement is a check of the reading. The relation of the conclusions ranges over the closure because the eraser marks and erases over the closure: its oracle unfolds the definitions of the list it reads, and a marking over the program can differ from the marking over the closure (DV-41); a \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} constant is found by its kername (DV-14), and kernames are injective only where \leandecl{Erasure.collectDeps} checks it, on the closure, which is what the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} environment the eraser emits holds. The view is outside what con-leche checks.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} con-leche's frontend on an export of the program, which is IO code (check C6) and not a function of the records; reading the records without checks, under which \texttt{collectDeps\_\allowbreak{}sub\_\allowbreak{}statement} is false on records con-leche does not read; one environment for acceptance and evaluation, which fails for programs whose names collide outside the closure; the erasure relation of the conclusions over the program, which needs the agreement of the oracle's marking over the closure and over the program that DV-41 names (about 2500 to 2900 lines).
\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-10}{DV-10}}\label{reg:dv-10}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Spec.lean}, \leandecl{EraseProof.EvalEnv.unfold?}: the source semantics unfolds definitions only; an opaque constant has no \ensuremath{\delta} rule.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}delta} (\texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICWcbvEval.v:247}; MC \S{}5.6), which unfolds every constant whose declaration has a body.
\item \textbf{What differs:} a Lean \texttt{opaque} declaration has a value, and the eraser emits it as the body of its \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} constant, but \leandecl{EraseProof.EvalEnv.unfold?} does not unfold it: evaluation is stuck where \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} evaluation unfolds.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} con-leche checks the value of an opaque against its type and stores the constant as an axiom, without the value (CL ConLeche/Kernel/Checker.lean:89 checkOpaqueVal), so its model of the environment relates the constant to no unfolding: the meaning claim \texttt{Sound} would be false for a step that replaces the constant by its value.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} unfolding opaques as \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}delta} does, under which evaluation does not preserve the meaning of the input in every model of the environment.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-11}{DV-11}}\label{reg:dv-11}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Spec.lean}: \leandecl{EraseProof.EvalEnv.isAtom} with \leandecl{EraseProof.EvidentZero}, \leandecl{EraseProof.DeltaFree}, \leandecl{EraseProof.EvidentProp} and \leandecl{EraseProof.IsThm}, the rule \leandecl{EraseProof.SrcEval.constAtom}; and the premise \texttt{\ensuremath{\sigma}.isAtom c = false} of \leandecl{EraseProof.Erases.const}: atoms erase only to \texttt{\ensuremath{\Box}}.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} PCUIC's atoms \texttt{atom} (\texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICWcbvEval.v:51}), which contain the inductive types \texttt{tInd}, and \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}atom} (\texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICWcbvEval.v:331}); a constant without a body has no rule. \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}tConst} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}Extract.v:104}) relates every constant to its \texttt{tConst}; \texttt{tInd} erases only to \texttt{\ensuremath{\Box}} (\texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}box}, \texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}Extract.v:140}).
\item \textbf{What differs:} a constant without a \ensuremath{\delta} rule (an axiom, an opaque, a theorem, an inductive type) is a value when its declared type is evidently an arity (\leandecl{Erasure.arityShape}), evidently a proposition (\leandecl{EraseProof.EvidentProp}), or it is a theorem; the spines it heads are values. Every other constant without a \ensuremath{\delta} rule is stuck.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} Lean's inductive types are constants, where PCUIC has the term \texttt{tInd}; and lemmas passed as arguments (theorems have no \ensuremath{\delta} here, DV-24) must be values, or the theorem is vacuous for every program that passes one. Atomhood is decided on declared types so that an atom's erasure, \texttt{\ensuremath{\Box}}, does not depend on the occurrence.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} every \ensuremath{\delta}-free constant a value: an axiom \texttt{n : Nat} would then be a value whose erasure, a \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} constant without a body, is not a \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} value (and con-leche declines such an axiom, DV-36); no \ensuremath{\delta}-free constant a value, under which programs that pass lemmas never evaluate.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-12}{DV-12}}\label{reg:dv-12}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Spec.lean}: \leandecl{EraseProof.EvalEnv} with its field \texttt{axiomatized}, \leandecl{EraseProof.EvalEnv.unfold?}, \leandecl{EraseProof.evalEnvOf} (the shipping test \leandecl{Erasure.axiomatized}), and the remapped branch of \leandecl{EraseProof.ErasesDecl}.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} \texttt{eval} (\texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICWcbvEval.v:231}), whose \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}delta} unfolds a constant exactly when it has a body, and \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}constant\_\allowbreak{}body} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}Extract.v:264}).
\item \textbf{What differs:} a definition that the configuration remaps to foreign code (\texttt{@[extern]} under \texttt{extern := .preferAxiom}) has a Lean value but no \ensuremath{\delta} rule, and \leandecl{EraseProof.ErasesDecl} relates it to a \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} declaration without a body, a pair \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}constant\_\allowbreak{}body} excludes. The source leaves the constant stuck. \leandecl{EraseProof.NoPreDefs} exempts such a declaration (the traversal gives it no body), so a remapped recursive definition is not excluded by DV-35.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} the eraser emits such a declaration as a \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} axiom so that it is linked with its foreign implementation; neither con-leche nor \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} models that implementation, so the source can only leave the constant stuck, as \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} leaves the axiom.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} excluding programs that mention a remapped constant, which also excludes programs that never evaluate it.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-13}{DV-13}}\label{reg:dv-13}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Spec.lean}: \leandecl{EraseProof.Fresh}, \leandecl{EraseProof.absFV} and the rule \leandecl{EraseProof.Erases.fvar}: the eraser's free variables, kept in the marking and related to themselves in \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box}; \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Target.lean}, \leandecl{EraseProof.hasFVar} and \leandecl{EraseProof.LenvClosed}: no body of the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} environment has a free variable.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} PCUIC's de Bruijn contexts and MetaRocq's \texttt{erase} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ErasureFunction.v:989}), which works on de Bruijn indices; \texttt{closed\_\allowbreak{}env} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}EGlobalEnv.v:181}).
\item \textbf{What differs:} the shipping traversal is locally nameless: it opens binders with free variables and closes them with \texttt{abstract} before a body is stored. \leandecl{EraseProof.MarkOf} opens each binder with a fresh free variable and closes it again, the erasure relation has a rule for free variables, and the closedness of the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} environment includes the absence of free variables. The input and the declarations have none (\texttt{toCL?} is \texttt{none} on a free variable, DV-1; \leandecl{EraseProof.ClosedDecls}).
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} the theorem is about the shipping traversal, which uses Lean's locally nameless \texttt{Expr} interface (\leanfile{LeanToLambdaBox/\allowbreak{}Erasure/\allowbreak{}Pure.lean}); its intermediate states contain free variables, which the induction over the traversal must relate.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} a relation on closed terms only, under which no intermediate state of the traversal is related.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-14}{DV-14}}\label{reg:dv-14}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Spec.lean}: the rule \leandecl{EraseProof.ErasesDeps.const}, indexed by the source constant \texttt{c} and finding its \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} declaration at \texttt{toKername c}; \leandecl{EraseProof.KernameInj} and \leandecl{EraseProof.BlockNamesInj}, hypotheses of \leandecl{EraseProof.erases_correct_statement}; \leandecl{EraseProof.BlockNamesInj}, a hypothesis of \leandecl{EraseProof.collectDeps_ok_of_statement}.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}deps\_\allowbreak{}tConst} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}Extract.v:324}; MC \S{}7.4), where the PCUIC and the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} declaration are found at the same kername.
\item \textbf{What differs:} a Lean constant and its \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} constant have different names (\texttt{toKername}), and two Lean names may have the same kername, so the rule names the source declaration it uses, and the simulation assumes that kernames are distinct on the evaluation environment and that no two \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} declarations of the closure share a name (\texttt{BlockNamesInj}).
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} \texttt{toKername} (\leanfile{LeanToLambdaBox/\allowbreak{}Basic.lean}) is not injective; the fragment test rejects closures with two constants or two \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} blocks of one kername (\leandecl{Erasure.findCollision}, \leandecl{Erasure.findBlockCollision}), so the hypotheses hold on what the eraser erases.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} an injective name mangling, a shipping change that alters the output for every name with special characters, which the theorem does not need.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-16}{DV-16}}\label{reg:dv-16}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Target.lean}: \leandecl{EraseProof.LBEval} with \leandecl{EraseProof.lbAtom}, \leandecl{EraseProof.csubst}, \leandecl{EraseProof.closedn}, \leandecl{EraseProof.hasFVar} and \leandecl{EraseProof.LenvClosed}, on the shipping AST \texttt{LBTerm} (\leanfile{LeanToLambdaBox/\allowbreak{}Basic.lean}); \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Spec.lean}, \leandecl{EraseProof.ErasesDeps} on the same terms.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} MetaRocq's \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} evaluation \texttt{eval} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}EWcbvEval.v:119}) on \texttt{term} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}EAst.v:29}), with \texttt{atom} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}EWcbvEval.v:36}), \texttt{csubst} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ECSubst.v:14}), \texttt{closedn} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ELiftSubst.v:90}) and \texttt{closed\_\allowbreak{}env} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}EGlobalEnv.v:181}); \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}deps} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}Extract.v:306}); MC \S{}7.1.
\item \textbf{What differs:} \texttt{LBTerm} has no \texttt{tVar}, \texttt{tEvar}, \texttt{tCoFix}, \texttt{tLazy} or \texttt{tForce}, and its only primitive values are 63-bit integers, so \leandecl{EraseProof.LBEval} has no cofixpoint or \texttt{force} rule; it has a constructor \texttt{fvar} (DV-13), with no evaluation rule. \leandecl{EraseProof.ErasesDeps} has no rule for primitive values, which the fragment does not produce (DV-26).
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} the theorem is about the eraser's output, an \texttt{LBTerm}, the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} that peregrine reads; the missing terms cannot occur in it.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} extending \texttt{LBTerm}, a shipping change no output needs; a separate transcription of \texttt{term}, which every statement would reach through a translation.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-17}{DV-17}}\label{reg:dv-17}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Statements.lean}: \leandecl{EraseProof.erase_correct_statement} assumes a run of \leandecl{Erasure.eraseEntry} that returns a program (\texttt{hrun}) and an evaluation of the source (\texttt{hev}); \leandecl{EraseProof.collectDeps_ok_of_statement} bounds the closure by the fragment test's fuel (\texttt{decls.length \ensuremath{\le} collectFuel}). The shipping oracle, fragment test and traversal are fuelled (\leandecl{Erasure.oracleFuel}, \leandecl{Erasure.collectFuel}, \leandecl{Erasure.travFuel}); \leandecl{EraseProof.CLTyped} asks con-leche's inference to accept at some fuel.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} MetaRocq's \texttt{is\_\allowbreak{}erasableb} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ErasureFunction.v:894}) and \texttt{erase} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ErasureFunction.v:989}; MC \S{}7.2), total under the hypothesis \texttt{NormalizationIn} (\texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICSN.v:44}); \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}erase} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ErasureFunction.v:1228}) and \texttt{erase\_\allowbreak{}correct} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ErasureFunctionProperties.v:657}), which hold for every input.
\item \textbf{What differs:} the final theorem is partial correctness: it says nothing about a run that fails (out of fuel, for example, an error of \texttt{\#erase} and never an output) and nothing about a source term that does not evaluate. No statement has a normalization hypothesis.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} con-leche proves no normalization: its theory is a set model, in which a term denotes a set, and its checker is fuelled, so a total oracle by well-founded recursion cannot be defined from its results, and a normalization hypothesis would stand in for a theorem con-leche does not have. For the same reason \leandecl{EraseProof.SrcEval} is tied to con-leche only through run-time certificates and the meaning claim \leandecl{EraseProof.Sound}, and nothing shows that a typed program evaluates.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} a normalization hypothesis as MetaRocq's \texttt{NormalizationIn}, which would assume what con-leche does not prove.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-23}{DV-23}}\label{reg:dv-23}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Spec.lean}: \leandecl{EraseProof.markEta} and the rules \leandecl{EraseProof.MarkEta.intro} and \leandecl{EraseProof.MarkAlt.intro} of the marking, which write each \ensuremath{\eta}-expansion the traversal performs (\texttt{withAppEtaToMinArity}, \texttt{lambdaMonocularOrIntro}) on the source term as an \texttt{eta}-marked \ensuremath{\lambda}; the rules \leandecl{EraseProof.SrcEval.etaLam} and \leandecl{EraseProof.SrcEval.etaBeta} (an \texttt{eta}-marked \ensuremath{\lambda} is a value and is applied as a \ensuremath{\lambda}); \leandecl{EraseProof.Erases.etaLam} and \leandecl{EraseProof.ErasesAlt.etaLam}; \leandecl{EraseProof.unmark}, which \ensuremath{\eta}-contracts the \texttt{eta} marks (\leandecl{EraseProof.etaContract}).
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} PCUIC's \texttt{eval} evaluates the arguments of an application eagerly (\texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}app\_\allowbreak{}cong}, \texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICWcbvEval.v:311}; \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}construct}, \texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICWcbvEval.v:303}); MetaRocq \ensuremath{\eta}-expands constructors in \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} by a separate pass (\texttt{isEtaExp}, \texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}EEtaExpanded.v:61}).
\item \textbf{What differs:} an under-applied constructor, \texttt{casesOn}, quotient or recursor spine is \ensuremath{\eta}-expanded in the marked input, one \texttt{eta}-marked \ensuremath{\lambda} per missing argument, and the expansion is the term that evaluates and is erased: its \ensuremath{\lambda} keeps the arguments as they are, and the erasure relates it to a \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} \ensuremath{\lambda}. No evaluation rule expands a spine and no erasure rule expands one.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} the eraser \ensuremath{\eta}-expands such spines, and the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} value of the expansion is a closure whose arguments are not evaluated; with eager evaluation of the unexpanded spine the source value has an evaluated argument where the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} value has the unevaluated one, and the final theorem is false (on \texttt{P2.mk ((fun x =\textgreater{} x) B.t)}). The expansion is written on the source term because con-leche gives meaning to a term only once its checker has typed it: \texttt{ProgCert} types the marked input as a whole (\leandecl{EraseProof.CLTypedAt}, so that the domain of each introduced binder is checked against the argument position it fills), and \texttt{unmark} \ensuremath{\eta}-contracts only \texttt{eta} marks, so that \texttt{Sound} compares the value with the unexpanded input.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} PCUIC's eager evaluation, under which the final theorem is false on under-applied constructors; an evaluation rule that expands a short spine, which has no mark for \texttt{ProgCert} to certify and no \ensuremath{\eta}-contraction for \texttt{unmark} to undo; an \ensuremath{\eta}-expansion pass on the source before evaluation, which is not what the eraser runs.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-24}{DV-24}}\label{reg:dv-24}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Spec.lean}: \leandecl{EraseProof.EvalEnv.unfold?} (no \ensuremath{\delta} for theorems), \leandecl{EraseProof.IsThm} in \leandecl{EraseProof.EvalEnv.isAtom} (theorems are atoms), and the rules \leandecl{EraseProof.SrcEval.projFrozen} and \leandecl{EraseProof.SrcEval.casesFrozen}, which handle the proofs the traversal erases (frozen, DV-32).
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}delta} (\texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICWcbvEval.v:247}), which unfolds a lemma like any constant with a body; \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box}'s \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}iota\_\allowbreak{}sing} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}EWcbvEval.v:162}) and \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}proj\_\allowbreak{}prop} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}EWcbvEval.v:238}), which reduce a \texttt{case} or a projection on a proof erased to \texttt{\ensuremath{\Box}}.
\item \textbf{What differs:} theorems are not unfolded, so a proof is a frozen term (when the traversal erases it) or an atom spine, never a constructor. A projection of a \texttt{Prop} structure out of a frozen proof is frozen (\texttt{projFrozen}), and a \texttt{casesOn} that the traversal reduces at erasure time continues with its alternative at frozen projections of its discriminant (\texttt{casesFrozen}, DV-25). A \texttt{casesOn} on a lemma of an inductive with proof fields that the traversal does not reduce does not evaluate, nor does a recursor on a lemma (\texttt{True.rec}, \texttt{And.rec} or \texttt{PUnit.rec.\{\_\allowbreak{}, 0\}} applied to a theorem): \leandecl{EraseProof.SrcEval.recIota} needs a constructor value as its major premise (DV-30), while \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} reduces the erased fixpoint's \texttt{case} on \texttt{\ensuremath{\Box}}. Programs defined by well-founded recursion, whose recursion reduces only through a proof of accessibility, do not evaluate either: the final theorem holds vacuously for all of these, and the fragment test excludes the last (DV-26).
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} con-leche stores a theorem by its statement alone, without its value (CL ConLeche/Kernel/Checker.lean:59 checkThmVal): its model has no unfolding of a theorem, and the value of a theorem typically uses recursors and tactics that nothing here evaluates.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} \ensuremath{\delta} for theorems, which has no counterpart in con-leche's environment; a recursor rule on a lemma, which covers only recursors of a field-less \texttt{Prop} constructor (\texttt{True.rec}; \texttt{And.rec} on a lemma stays stuck as \texttt{And.casesOn} does) and needs its own run-time certificate.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-25}{DV-25}}\label{reg:dv-25}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Spec.lean}: \leandecl{EraseProof.EvalEnv.casesOn?} (the shipping recognizer \leandecl{Erasure.casesInfo?}), the rules \leandecl{EraseProof.SrcEval.casesIota}, \leandecl{EraseProof.SrcEval.casesLitZero}, \leandecl{EraseProof.SrcEval.casesLitSucc} and \leandecl{EraseProof.SrcEval.casesFrozen}; the marks \leandecl{EraseProof.markReduced} and \leandecl{EraseProof.MarkSat.casesReduced}; the rules \leandecl{EraseProof.Erases.cases} and \leandecl{EraseProof.Erases.casesReduced}.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} PCUIC's \texttt{tCase}, a term, with \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}iota} (\texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICWcbvEval.v:253}); \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}tCase} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}Extract.v:109}); \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box}'s \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}iota\_\allowbreak{}sing} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}EWcbvEval.v:162}).
\item \textbf{What differs:} Lean has no case term: \texttt{T.casesOn} is a definition through the recursor \texttt{T.rec}. The source treats a recognized \texttt{casesOn} as primitive, without \ensuremath{\delta}, reducing on the constructor its major evaluates to; it does not unfold it to the recursor, which has a rule of its own (\leandecl{EraseProof.SrcEval.recIota}, DV-30). A \texttt{casesOn} on a one-constructor inductive whose sort may be \texttt{Prop} is reduced by the traversal at erasure time: the discriminant is marked \texttt{reduced}, it is not evaluated, con-leche certifies it as a proof (\leandecl{EraseProof.CLErasable} in \texttt{casesFrozen}, \leandecl{EraseProof.CLCert} in \texttt{casesReduced}), and the erased alternative is applied to \texttt{\ensuremath{\Box}} for each field, the reduction \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}iota\_\allowbreak{}sing} makes at run time. The fragment test admits it only on an inductive written in \texttt{Prop} (\leandecl{Erasure.eliminatedUndecided}), whose fields are proofs.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} the eraser translates recognized \texttt{casesOn} spines to \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} \texttt{case} and never unfolds them (\leanfile{LeanToLambdaBox/\allowbreak{}Erasure.lean}); a recursor it erases to a \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} fixpoint of its own (DV-30), not to a \texttt{case}. The reduced form is what the eraser emits when the discriminant's sort may be \texttt{Prop}, since \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} marks a whole block as propositional or not; without a typing, the premise that the discriminant is a proof is a certificate of con-leche's checker.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} \ensuremath{\delta}-unfolding \texttt{casesOn} to \texttt{T.rec} and evaluating the recursor, which has no counterpart in the eraser's output.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-26}{DV-26}}\label{reg:dv-26}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Statements.lean}: the hypothesis \texttt{hfrag} of \leandecl{EraseProof.erase_correct_statement}, that the shipping fragment test \leandecl{Erasure.collectDeps} accepts the input; and \leandecl{EraseProof.collectDeps_ok_of_statement}, a sufficient condition for it (\leandecl{EraseProof.ReadClosed}, \leandecl{EraseProof.PhaseIDecl}, \leandecl{EraseProof.PlainExpr}, \leandecl{EraseProof.RecShaped}, \leandecl{EraseProof.PreRead}, \leandecl{EraseProof.KernameInj}, \leandecl{EraseProof.BlockNamesInj}), which covers the recursors and the structural recursion that the test admits.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} MetaRocq's \texttt{erase\_\allowbreak{}correct} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ErasureFunctionProperties.v:657}), which holds for every well-typed term.
\item \textbf{What differs:} the final theorem covers the inputs the fragment test accepts and con-leche accepts. The fragment test's exclusion classes: recursors that a read expression names other than those of a single inductive without indices that eliminates into every sort and whose induction hypotheses take no arguments and are about the last fields (\leandecl{EraseProof.RecInFragment}; \leandecl{Erasure.recShapeInFragment}), and those the eraser keeps as constants (\leandecl{Erasure.recStaysConstant}); recursive definitions (every definition with a compiled \texttt{\_\allowbreak{}unsafe\_\allowbreak{}rec} companion except one that \leandecl{Erasure.isStructuralRecursive} recognizes, a syntactic test for a \texttt{T.brecOn} in its value; definitions by well-founded recursion and \texttt{partial} definitions are out); definitions, theorems and opaques of mutual blocks, \texttt{partial}, \texttt{unsafe} and \texttt{implemented\_\allowbreak{}by} constants, nested inductives, string literals, Nat literals and Nat or Int constructors under \texttt{nat := .machine}, \texttt{casesOn} on a constructor with an index field, eliminations of an inductive whose sort may be both \texttt{Prop} and not \texttt{Prop}, \texttt{remove\_\allowbreak{}irrel\_\allowbreak{}constr\_\allowbreak{}args}, metavariables. The hypotheses of the final theorem add the classes that con-leche or the source semantics leaves out: user axioms (DV-36), declarations of \texttt{Nat.div} and \texttt{Nat.mod} (DV-38), and structural recursion through compiled pre-definitions, the default \texttt{structural := .unsafeRec} (DV-35).
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} \texttt{\#erase} sends an input outside the fragment to the \texttt{Meta} path (\leandecl{Erasure.route}, \leanloc{LeanToLambdaBox/\allowbreak{}Erasure/\allowbreak{}Entry.lean}{331-335}), \texttt{CoreM} code about which nothing is proved, and some of the excluded constructs have no con-leche counterpart (\texttt{unsafe} and \texttt{partial} constants). Typed inputs outside the fragment exist, so the hypothesis cannot be derived from typing as in the lean4lean experiment.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} deriving the hypothesis from \texttt{hacc}, \texttt{hview} and \texttt{hty}, which is false on typed programs that use a mutual recursor; leaving the fragment unstated, which makes it impossible to tell how much the hypothesis excludes, which \leandecl{EraseProof.collectDeps_ok_of_statement} states.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-27}{DV-27}}\label{reg:dv-27}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Spec.lean}: \leandecl{EraseProof.FirstOrderValue}, the values on which \leandecl{EraseProof.erase_correct_firstorder_statement} determines the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} value, their structural erasure \leandecl{EraseProof.foErase} (with \leandecl{EraseProof.peanoLB}), and \leandecl{EraseProof.FrozenLeaf}.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} \texttt{firstorder\_\allowbreak{}value} (\texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICFirstorder.v:115}), with the first-order inductives of \texttt{firstorder\_\allowbreak{}con} (\texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICFirstorder.v:52}), and \texttt{erase\_\allowbreak{}correct\_\allowbreak{}strong} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ErasureFunctionProperties.v:2269}).
\item \textbf{What differs:} MetaRocq's first-order value is a typed constructor application of an inductive that is not propositional, every argument (parameters included) a first-order value, and its first-order inductives have neither type parameters nor proof fields. Ours is syntactic: a tree of saturated constructor applications whose leaves are frozen terms (\texttt{markErase}, erased to \texttt{\ensuremath{\Box}}: type parameters and proof fields the traversal erased) and Nat literals (erased to Peano numerals). The conclusion compares with the structural erasure, which keeps parameters (DV-23), instead of the erasure function's output, and adds that con-leche types the value (\leandecl{EraseProof.CLTyped}) and certifies every frozen leaf (\leandecl{EraseProof.CLErasable}).
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} a Lean inductive in \texttt{Sort u} is universe-polymorphic over \texttt{Prop}, and there is no typing from which to read whether a constructor application is a proof: the marks are the eraser's decision, so a leaf erased to \texttt{\ensuremath{\Box}} is a mark, and a constructor node is unmarked and erases to a \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} constructor. \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} keeps parameters in constructor applications (DV-23), and Lean's data inductives take type parameters (\texttt{Prod}, \texttt{Option}, \texttt{List}) and its structures proof fields (\texttt{Subtype}, \texttt{Fin}), so MetaRocq's notion would leave only monomorphic inductives without proofs; there is no erasure function on the relation's side to compare with.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} MetaRocq's notion exactly (all arguments first-order, the inductive not propositional), which excludes every value with a type parameter; comparing with \leandecl{Erasure.erasePure}'s output, which reads the configuration and the view instead of the value alone.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-28}{DV-28}}\label{reg:dv-28}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Spec.lean}: \leandecl{EraseProof.ErasesAlt} (rules \texttt{done}, \texttt{lam} and \texttt{etaLam}) and \leandecl{EraseProof.MarkAlt.intro}.

The relation is as MetaRocq's.
