\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-29}{DV-29}}\label{reg:dv-29}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Spec.lean}: the rules \leandecl{EraseProof.SrcEval.quotMk} and \leandecl{EraseProof.SrcEval.quotLift}; \leandecl{EraseProof.quotEvalArity} in \leandecl{EraseProof.specialArity}, so that \leandecl{EraseProof.MarkEta.intro} \ensuremath{\eta}-expands \texttt{Quot.mk} and \texttt{Quot.lift} spines with missing arguments; the quotient clauses of \leandecl{EraseProof.OwnRules}, under which \leandecl{EraseProof.EvalEnv.isAtom} makes the type former \texttt{Quot} an atom, and of \leandecl{EraseProof.BlocksCong} (\texttt{Quot.mk} spines); the rules \leandecl{EraseProof.Erases.quotMk} and \leandecl{EraseProof.Erases.quotLift}.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} none: PCUIC has no primitive quotients. The closest rules are \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}beta} (\texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICWcbvEval.v:234}) and \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}construct} (\texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICWcbvEval.v:303}) of \texttt{eval}, and \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}tApp} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}Extract.v:101}) and \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}tConstruct} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}Extract.v:106}) of \texttt{erases}.
\item \textbf{What differs:} Lean's quotients are primitive constants with their own reduction, the quotient \ensuremath{\iota} \texttt{Quot.lift f h (Quot.mk r a) \ensuremath{\leadsto} f a}. The source evaluates \texttt{Quot.mk \ensuremath{\alpha} r a} by evaluating the element \texttt{a}, the type and the relation unevaluated, and \texttt{Quot.lift \ensuremath{\alpha} r \ensuremath{\beta} f h q} by evaluating \texttt{f} to a \ensuremath{\lambda} and \texttt{q} to \texttt{Quot.mk \ensuremath{\alpha}' r' a} and continuing with the \ensuremath{\lambda}'s body at \texttt{a}; each step carries the certificate \leandecl{EraseProof.CLOk} of the term it forms (DV-33). A \texttt{Quot.mk} value blocks application congruence as a constructor value does. The type former \texttt{Quot} is an atom, as an inductive type former is (DV-11): a quotient type \texttt{Quot \ensuremath{\alpha} r} evaluates its arguments by application congruence and is a value, so it may be a constructor parameter or a \ensuremath{\beta}-argument, and it erases only to \texttt{\ensuremath{\Box}}. \texttt{Quot.ind} has no rule: a program that evaluates it, for instance as an argument, is stuck, and the final theorem holds vacuously for it. The erasure represents a quotient by its elements: \texttt{Quot.mk \ensuremath{\alpha} r a} erases as \texttt{a} and \texttt{Quot.lift \ensuremath{\alpha} r \ensuremath{\beta} f h q} as \texttt{f q}, applied to the erasures of the arguments beyond the arity.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} the reference has no rule for quotients, and the eraser erases the quotient constants in this way, as Lean's code generator does (\texttt{visitConstApp}, \leanloc{LeanToLambdaBox/\allowbreak{}Erasure.lean}{958}). con-leche installs each quotient constant from its own pin (CL ConLeche/Kernel/Checker.lean:467 checkQuotRecord), so a program that mentions them is accepted with the constants' fixed types and its model interprets them; the source rules are the quotient \ensuremath{\iota} under call by value. \texttt{Quot.ind} is a proof, but its statement ends in an application of its motive and is not an evident proposition, so the oracle is not known to erase its spines and the eraser may keep it as a \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} axiom, while an atom erases only to \texttt{\ensuremath{\Box}}.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} erasing \texttt{Quot.mk} and \texttt{Quot.lift} to \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} axioms, under which every program that computes through a quotient is stuck in \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box}; no source rule for quotients, under which such programs do not evaluate and the final theorem says nothing about them.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-30}{DV-30}}\label{reg:dv-30}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Spec.lean}: the rule \leandecl{EraseProof.SrcEval.recIota} with \leandecl{EraseProof.natLitCtor}; the rules \leandecl{EraseProof.Erases.recLet} and \leandecl{EraseProof.Erases.recFix} with \leandecl{EraseProof.RecFixOf}, \leandecl{EraseProof.recMembers}, \leandecl{EraseProof.recLets} and \leandecl{EraseProof.EvalEnv.recBlock?}; the recursor clause of \leandecl{EraseProof.specialArity}; the recursor exclusion of \leandecl{EraseProof.Erases.const}; \leandecl{EraseProof.RecInFragment} in \leandecl{EraseProof.PhaseIDecl}; \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Target.lean}: \leandecl{EraseProof.lbLift} and \leandecl{EraseProof.LBFixed}.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} none: PCUIC has no recursors (eliminators are \texttt{tCase} and \texttt{tFix}). The closest rules are \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}fix} (\texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICWcbvEval.v:273}), \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}zeta} and \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}iota} of \texttt{eval}, and \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}tFix} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}Extract.v:122}), \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}tLetIn} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}Extract.v:96}) and \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}tCase} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}Extract.v:109}) of \texttt{erases}.
\item \textbf{What differs:} the source evaluates a saturated recursor \texttt{T.rec ps ms mins maj} of a single inductive \texttt{T} without indices, whose recursive fields take no arguments and come after the other fields of their constructor, by evaluating the minors to \texttt{mvs} and the major to a constructor value \texttt{C qs fs} (a Nat literal major is read as its constructor form \texttt{natLitCtor}: \texttt{0} as \texttt{Nat.zero}, \texttt{k + 1} as \texttt{Nat.succ} applied to the literal \texttt{k}, as Lean's kernel reads it), then each induction hypothesis \texttt{T.rec ps ms mvs f} (one per recursive field \texttt{f}, in the order of the minor's hypotheses) to a value, and continuing with the minor's value applied to the fields and these values; the step carries the certificate \leandecl{EraseProof.CLOk} of the recursor application with its evaluated minors and major (DV-33). The parameters and the motive are not evaluated. There is no source \ensuremath{\iota} for recursors of mutual, nested or indexed inductives, for higher-order recursive fields, for recursive fields before non-recursive ones, nor on a major that is not a constructor value (a frozen proof, a theorem: DV-24; \texttt{recK} and structure \ensuremath{\eta} are not rules). The fragment test admits exactly the recursors of this shape that the eraser does not keep as constants (\texttt{RecInFragment}). The erasure is the eraser's: the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} fixpoint of \texttt{recFix} under \texttt{let}s of the erased minors, applied to the erased major and the extra arguments (\texttt{Erases.recLet}); \texttt{Erases.recFix} relates the same fixpoint with closed \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} values of the minors substituted, the form \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} reaches after the \texttt{let}s and in which the recursive calls appear. The \texttt{direct} form of the fixpoint (alternatives applied to \texttt{\ensuremath{\Box}}) is admitted only for blocks whose one-constructor members are declared in \texttt{Prop} or have no fields, a declaration condition in place of a typing of the major.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} the reference has no recursors, and the eraser compiles them to \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} fixpoints (\texttt{visitRec}, \leanloc{LeanToLambdaBox/\allowbreak{}Erasure.lean}{1003}). \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} evaluates the minors (\texttt{let}) and every argument of an application by value, so the source evaluates the minors and the induction hypotheses first. Under \texttt{nat := .peano} the eraser emits a Nat literal as \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box}'s constructor chain (\texttt{visitLiteral}; \texttt{Erases.litZero}, \texttt{Erases.litSucc}), on which the erased fixpoint computes, and Lean's kernel reduces a recursor on a literal; without the reading of a literal major as its constructor form the source would be stuck on these programs (structural recursion on \texttt{2} included). The \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} rule \texttt{iota} needs a non-propositional block, and nothing types a constructor value of a \texttt{Prop} inductive, so the \texttt{direct} form rests on the declaration.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} a source \ensuremath{\iota} on the unevaluated induction hypotheses, under which the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} evaluation of a hypothesis the minor ignores has no source counterpart; erasing recursors to \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} axioms (as \texttt{recStaysConstant} does for the excluded cases), under which every program that computes through a recursor is stuck in \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box}; for a literal major, a source step \texttt{k + 1 \ensuremath{\leadsto} Nat.succ k} on literals, which would make a literal a non-value, or a separate rule repeating the premises of \texttt{recIota} (as \texttt{casesLitZero} and \texttt{casesLitSucc} do for \texttt{casesOn}).
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-31}{DV-31}}\label{reg:dv-31}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Spec.lean}, \leandecl{EraseProof.NoPreDefs}, the hypothesis \texttt{hnopre} of \leandecl{EraseProof.erase_correct_statement}.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} none: MetaRocq's \texttt{erase\_\allowbreak{}correct} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ErasureFunctionProperties.v:657}) has no counterpart, since a PCUIC environment holds the recursive definition itself.
\item \textbf{What differs:} Not applicable on this branch. The statement has no hypothesis on the pre-definitions of the program (no \texttt{PreDefsOK}, no typing of the \texttt{\_\allowbreak{}unsafe\_\allowbreak{}rec} companion): the declarations whose compiled pre-definition the traversal would erase are excluded (DV-35), and \leandecl{EraseProof.ViewAgrees} only places the constants the pre-definitions name in the program, for what the fragment test reads through the view (DV-3).
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} not applicable: the entry exists for the citations of the earlier registers.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} dropping the id, which would leave the earlier citations without an entry.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-32}{DV-32}}\label{reg:dv-32}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Spec.lean}: \leandecl{EraseProof.MarkOf} (with \leandecl{EraseProof.MarkEta}, \leandecl{EraseProof.MarkSat}, \leandecl{EraseProof.MarkAlt}, \leandecl{EraseProof.markErase}, \leandecl{EraseProof.markMD}), which writes the eraser's erasability decisions on the source term (hypothesis \texttt{hmark} of \leandecl{EraseProof.erase_correct_statement}); \leandecl{EraseProof.unmark}; the frozen rules of \leandecl{EraseProof.SrcEval}: \leandecl{EraseProof.SrcEval.frozen}, \leandecl{EraseProof.SrcEval.frozenApp}, \leandecl{EraseProof.SrcEval.projFrozen} and \leandecl{EraseProof.SrcEval.casesFrozen}; \leandecl{EraseProof.Erases.box}, which relates \texttt{\ensuremath{\Box}} to the \texttt{erase}-marked terms only; \leandecl{EraseProof.ArityTypes}; \leandecl{EraseProof.markOf_det_statement} and \leandecl{EraseProof.markOf_exists_statement}.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}box} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}Extract.v:140}) with \texttt{isErasable} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}Extract.v:18}), which relates \texttt{\ensuremath{\Box}} to every term whose type is a proof or an arity; \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}box} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}EWcbvEval.v:121}); the premises \texttt{wf\_\allowbreak{}ext \ensuremath{\Sigma}} and \texttt{welltyped \ensuremath{\Sigma} [] t} of \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}correct} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ErasureCorrectness.v:51}), and \texttt{ind\_\allowbreak{}arity\_\allowbreak{}eq} (\texttt{common/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}EnvironmentTyping.v:1651}) of a well-formed environment.
\item \textbf{What differs:} the source semantics evaluates the marked term, not the input. \texttt{MarkOf} is a function of the input and the closure (\texttt{markOf\_\allowbreak{}det\_\allowbreak{}statement}: for a closure whose types and values mention no free variable, and a closed input at no locals, two markings of the input are equal), defined wherever the traversal runs on the closure of a program con-leche accepts (\texttt{markOf\_\allowbreak{}exists\_\allowbreak{}statement}); every node the traversal asks the oracle about is marked \texttt{erase} when the oracle answers \texttt{true}. A frozen subterm is a value (\texttt{frozen}), no rule evaluates inside it, a frozen function applied is frozen (\texttt{frozenApp}, \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box}'s \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}box}), a projection of a frozen proof is frozen (\texttt{projFrozen}), a \texttt{casesOn} reduced at erasure time continues at frozen projections (\texttt{casesFrozen}, DV-25). \texttt{Erases.box} relates \texttt{\ensuremath{\Box}} to exactly the \texttt{erase}-marked terms and asks the certificate \texttt{cert} of the mark (DV-37) where MetaRocq asks \texttt{isErasable}; \texttt{unmark} removes the marks. \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}correct\_\allowbreak{}statement} has no \texttt{wf\_\allowbreak{}ext}, no \texttt{welltyped} and no typing premise; it has \texttt{ArityTypes} (the declared type of every inductive of the closure is syntactically an arity, \leandecl{Erasure.arityShape}) where a well-formed environment gives \texttt{ind\_\allowbreak{}arity\_\allowbreak{}eq}, besides \texttt{KernameInj}, \texttt{BlockNamesInj} (DV-14) and \texttt{LenvClosed} (DV-13). The oracle \leandecl{Erasure.Pure.isErasable} defines the marks and is not verified; the statement reads it through \texttt{MarkOf}, so a change to the oracle changes the statement (\texttt{proof/\allowbreak{}spec.pin} pins it by digest). The theorem does not prove that the erased subterms are irrelevant to the computation: if the eraser erases a subterm the computation needs, the marked evaluation is stuck or \texttt{hcert} fails, and the theorem says nothing about that program.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} con-leche has no typing judgement and no subject reduction, so \texttt{isErasable \ensuremath{\Sigma} \ensuremath{\Gamma} t} (a typing statement) cannot be asked, and the premises \texttt{wf\_\allowbreak{}ext} and \texttt{welltyped} have no counterpart (\leandecl{EraseProof.ConLecheAccepts} and \leandecl{EraseProof.CLTyped} are runs of the checker, DV-1, DV-38). The semantic substitute is not available: con-leche's model does not separate type formers from data (\texttt{Nat.zero}, the type \texttt{Empty} and \texttt{PUnit.unit.\{1\}} have one denotation, CL ConLeche/SetModel/Value.lean:625 bval), so "t is erased" cannot be a property of what t denotes. Evaluating inside an erased subterm would give the subterm a meaning to preserve and a run to evaluate, which types and proofs under binders do not have; freezing it makes \texttt{\ensuremath{\Box}} match \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}box} and leaves the meaning claim to the certificate (DV-37).
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} semantic erasability in the model, which is false for types (no separation of type formers from data); \texttt{ErasableS}-style typing on Lean terms, which no development of this repository provides for con-leche; no marks, evaluating the erased subterms, under which \texttt{hev} is unsatisfiable on programs with an erased type or proof argument; verifying the oracle, which needs a typing metatheory for Lean that con-leche does not have.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-33}{DV-33}}\label{reg:dv-33}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Spec.lean}: \leandecl{EraseProof.CLOk} and \leandecl{EraseProof.CLErasable} as premises of the rules of \leandecl{EraseProof.SrcEval}: \leandecl{EraseProof.SrcEval.beta}, \leandecl{EraseProof.SrcEval.etaBeta}, \leandecl{EraseProof.SrcEval.zeta}, \leandecl{EraseProof.SrcEval.ctor}, \leandecl{EraseProof.SrcEval.casesIota}, \leandecl{EraseProof.SrcEval.quotMk}, \leandecl{EraseProof.SrcEval.quotLift}, \leandecl{EraseProof.SrcEval.recIota}, \leandecl{EraseProof.SrcEval.proj}, \leandecl{EraseProof.SrcEval.lit} and \leandecl{EraseProof.SrcEval.appCong} ask \texttt{CLOk}; \leandecl{EraseProof.SrcEval.frozen}, \texttt{frozenApp}, \texttt{projFrozen} and \texttt{casesFrozen} ask \texttt{CLErasable}.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} \texttt{eval} (\texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICWcbvEval.v:231}) has no typing premise; \texttt{subject\_\allowbreak{}reduction\_\allowbreak{}eval} (\texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICClassification.v:1093}) derives the typing of the value from that of the input.
\item \textbf{What differs:} a rule that forms a redex or a data value from evaluated parts asks con-leche's inference to accept the closed term it forms (\texttt{CLOk}, which is \leandecl{EraseProof.CLTyped}); a rule that freezes a term asks con-leche to type it as a proof or a type former (\texttt{CLErasable}). The hypothesis \texttt{hev} of the final theorem is therefore an evaluation together with a list of runs of con-leche's checker, one per step.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} con-leche gives a meaning only to the terms its checker has typed (a term inferred to have a type denotes a member of it, \texttt{CL ConLeche/\allowbreak{}Model/\allowbreak{}Claims.lean:112 InferClaim}), and it has no subject reduction by which the typing of the contractum would follow from that of the redex. \leandecl{EraseProof.Sound} is proved from these certificates, step by step.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} no certificate, which leaves \texttt{Sound} without a reason that each intermediate term denotes anything; proving subject reduction for con-leche's checker, a syntactic metatheory that its theory does not contain.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-34}{DV-34}}\label{reg:dv-34}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Spec.lean}: \leandecl{EraseProof.Sound} (with \leandecl{EraseProof.CLStrictType}), the conclusion of \leandecl{EraseProof.srcEval_sound_statement} and the last conjunct of \leandecl{EraseProof.erase_correct_statement}; \leandecl{EraseProof.sound_nonvacuous_statement}.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} subject reduction: \texttt{subject\_\allowbreak{}reduction} (\texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICSR.v:3129}) and \texttt{subject\_\allowbreak{}reduction\_\allowbreak{}eval} (\texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICClassification.v:1093}), which \texttt{erase\_\allowbreak{}correct} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ErasureFunctionProperties.v:657}) uses to type the value that \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}correct} relates to the erased one.
\item \textbf{What differs:} the final theorem concludes \texttt{Sound env e v}: the unmarked value has a con-leche reading, and in every model of the accepted environment (every \texttt{V} with \texttt{[SetTheory V]}, every \leandecl{ConLeche.Model.EnvModelM} model, level valuation and variable assignment) it denotes what the input denotes, provided that is not the proof point. It is not type preservation: con-leche's model gives \texttt{Nat.zero}, the type \texttt{Empty} and \texttt{PUnit.unit.\{1\}} one denotation, so a value of another type with the input's denotation satisfies it; the value's type is fixed by \leandecl{EraseProof.SrcEval} and, for a first-order value, by \leandecl{EraseProof.CLTyped} on it. \texttt{SetTheory} is a hypothesis (an instance argument). \leandecl{EraseProof.sound_nonvacuous_statement} shows that the antecedent has content: if con-leche types an application of the input to closed arguments with a type whose whnf is a sort (\leandecl{EraseProof.CLStrictType}), the input has a reading in every model that is not the proof point. For a data-typed input, \leandecl{ConLeche.Model.EnvModelM} does not state that an inductive's carrier excludes the proof point: typing puts the carrier in a universe, which also holds the truth value whose member is the proof point (CL ConLeche/SetTheory/Derive/Univ.lean:53 mem\_univ\_of\_mem\_univZero); con-leche's construction makes it a tagged sum for the recorded blocks (\leandecl{ConLeche.Model.EnvModelM.lfp_ok}, CL ConLeche/Model/Env/EnvModelM.lean:316 lfp\_ok), and which blocks are recorded is carried by its fold beside the model (CL ConLeche/Model/Cover.lean:15 LfpCover), not stated by \leandecl{ConLeche.Model.EnvModelM}. So in such a model \texttt{Sound} can be vacuous for data: the input may denote the proof point there.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} con-leche's results are about denotations in its set model: its claims on head normalisation, definitional equality and inference preserve denotations (CL ConLeche/Model/Claims.lean:52 WhnfCoreClaim) and say nothing about proofs, which all denote the proof point (CL ConLeche/SetTheory/Derive/Pt.lean:69 pt); there is no typing judgement to preserve. A model exists only under an inaccessibility hypothesis that this development does not use, so the model is a hypothesis of the statement, as in \texttt{CL ConLeche/\allowbreak{}MainTheorem.lean:102 model\_\allowbreak{}exists}.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} type preservation, which needs a typing judgement and subject reduction; denotation equality unconditionally, which is false where the input denotes the proof point and the value is a term that does not.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-35}{DV-35}}\label{reg:dv-35}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Spec.lean}: \leandecl{EraseProof.NoPreDefs}, the hypothesis \texttt{hnopre} of \leandecl{EraseProof.erase_correct_statement}, with the premise in \leandecl{EraseProof.collectDeps_sub_statement} and \leandecl{EraseProof.erasePure_erases_statement}.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} none: MetaRocq's \texttt{erase\_\allowbreak{}correct} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ErasureFunctionProperties.v:657}) has no counterpart, since a PCUIC environment holds the recursive definition itself, evaluated by \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}fix} (\texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICWcbvEval.v:273}) and erased by \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}tFix} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}Extract.v:122}).
\item \textbf{What differs:} no declaration of the closure that the traversal erases by its value has a compiled pre-definition (\leandecl{Erasure.preDef?} is \texttt{none}); a remapped \texttt{@[extern]} definition (\leandecl{Erasure.axiomatized}) is exempt, since \texttt{visitMutual} gives it no body. A structurally recursive definition erased through its \texttt{\_\allowbreak{}unsafe\_\allowbreak{}rec} companion, which is the default \texttt{structural := .unsafeRec}, is therefore outside the theorem; under \texttt{structural := .kernel} it is inside, erased through its kernel value.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} the companion is a \texttt{partial} definition that con-leche does not read (\leandecl{EraseProof.DeclsOf?} leaves unsafe and partial constants out), so it has no denotation, and a source rule that unfolds it could not be proved to preserve the meaning of the input (\leandecl{EraseProof.Sound}).
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} a source rule that evaluates the companion and asks the conversion of its application with the constant's as a premise at each call, which gives the companion no denotation in con-leche's model; adding the companion to the program, which \texttt{DeclsOf?} skips as partial.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-36}{DV-36}}\label{reg:dv-36}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Spec.lean}: \leandecl{EraseProof.ConLecheAccepts} (hypothesis \texttt{hacc} of \leandecl{EraseProof.erase_correct_statement}), through \leandecl{EraseProof.DeclsOf?}, which passes every axiom record of the program to con-leche's fold.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} MetaRocq's \texttt{wf\_\allowbreak{}ext} (\texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICTyping.v:507}), which admits a constant without a body, and \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}constant\_\allowbreak{}body} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}Extract.v:264}), which relates it to a constant without a body.
\item \textbf{What differs:} a program with a user axiom is outside the theorem: con-leche installs only its pinned axioms (\texttt{propext}, \texttt{Classical.choice}, \texttt{Quot.sound} and the compiler-trust family \texttt{Lean.trustCompiler}, \texttt{Lean.ofReduceBool}, \texttt{Lean.ofReduceNat}) and tolerates a declared, unused \texttt{sorryAx} (CL ConLeche/Kernel/CheckDecl.lean:88-102); its fold declines any other axiom, so \texttt{hacc} is false of such a program. Axioms that a program mentions without declaring them are the pinned ones.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} con-leche's model gives a meaning to an axiom only for the ones it pins; an arbitrary axiom has none, and the statement is about con-leche's acceptance.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} admitting user axioms as atoms (DV-11), under which \texttt{hacc} is unsatisfiable on every program that declares one, so the theorem would hold vacuously for them without saying so.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-37}{DV-37}}\label{reg:dv-37}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Spec.lean}: \leandecl{EraseProof.CLCert} (with \leandecl{EraseProof.CLVerdict}, \leandecl{EraseProof.CLFormer}, \leandecl{EraseProof.CLProof}, \leandecl{EraseProof.lamTele}, \leandecl{EraseProof.openLams}, \leandecl{EraseProof.CLTypedAt}), \leandecl{EraseProof.MarksCert} and \leandecl{EraseProof.ProgCert}, the hypothesis \texttt{hcert} of \leandecl{EraseProof.erase_correct_statement}, \leandecl{EraseProof.ValuesMarkedOf} (a premise of \leandecl{EraseProof.erasePure_erases_statement}, and the hypothesis \texttt{hvals} of \leandecl{EraseProof.erase_correct_firstorder_statement}), \leandecl{EraseProof.ErasedValue} (read by both and by \leandecl{EraseProof.ErasesDecl}), and \leandecl{EraseProof.clCert_proof_pt_statement}.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} \texttt{isErasable} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}Extract.v:18}), asked of every \texttt{\ensuremath{\Box}} by \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}box} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}Extract.v:140}) and computed by \texttt{is\_\allowbreak{}erasableb} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ErasureFunction.v:894}) with a type inference; MC \S{}7.2.
\item \textbf{What differs:} the erased subterms are certified by runs of con-leche's checker on the given program, not by a typing derivation. \texttt{ProgCert} asks that con-leche types the marked input as a whole and a marking of the value of every constant of the closure that the traversal erases (\leandecl{EraseProof.CLTypedAt}), and that every \texttt{erase} mark and the discriminant of every \texttt{reduced} mark is certified in the context of its enclosing binders (\texttt{MarksCert}): the closed telescope of its binders is typed, and the subterm opened as con-leche opens binders has a type that is a proposition (\texttt{CLProof}: the subterm then denotes the proof point in every model, \leandecl{EraseProof.clCert_proof_pt_statement}) or a type-former type (\texttt{CLFormer}, the checker's own reducing test, a syntactic verdict with no model content). The checks run at the checker's fuel \texttt{checkFuel} and are decidable. A \texttt{\ensuremath{\Box}} of the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} value under a binder is a certified mark with evaluated values substituted, which no check repeats. The \texttt{\ensuremath{\Box}}s that the relation does not pair with a mark (the direct-mode placeholders of a recursor's fixpoint, DV-30) rest on declaration conditions and the fragment test, not on a certificate. The oracle's answers are checked on this program, not proved. The value conjunct of \leandecl{EraseProof.erase_correct_statement} relates the \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} value with \leandecl{EraseProof.Erases} at \leandecl{EraseProof.noCert}, not at the certificate: MetaRocq's \texttt{erases\_\allowbreak{}correct} relates it by \texttt{erases}, with \texttt{isErasable} at every \texttt{\ensuremath{\Box}}. The certificate is a fuelled con-leche run with no substitution lemma, so it is not carried to substituted values. The values certified are those of the closure that the traversal erases (\leandecl{EraseProof.ErasedValue}: a definition that is not a \texttt{casesOn} that \leandecl{Erasure.casesInfo?} recognizes, or an opaque; never a theorem, on whose spines the oracle answers \texttt{true} before it reads anything else), also those whose body the emitted \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} environment does not hold: a program on which the oracle has no marking of such a value, or con-leche does not certify it, is outside the theorem.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} con-leche has neither a typing judgement nor a semantic criterion for type formers (DV-32), so \texttt{isErasable} can be replaced only by what its checker decides; the oracle (\leandecl{Erasure.Pure.isErasable}) is unverified, and the certificate recovers the property per program. The context of the binders is part of the check because con-leche types a term only closed, and the domain of a binder must itself be checked. The certificate covers every value of the closure that the traversal erases, whether or not the emitted environment holds its body, because the proof of \texttt{erasePure\_\allowbreak{}erases} needs a marking of each value the traversal erases (\texttt{ErasesDecl}, which records \texttt{ErasedValue}) before it relates the value's run to the emitted program, and the test is the traversal's own (\texttt{visitMutual} is reached only on such constants); its premise \texttt{ValuesMarkedOf} is the first component of \texttt{ProgCert}'s third conjunct. The first-order corollary has no certificate and takes \texttt{ValuesMarkedOf} itself (\texttt{hvals}), for the same reason: its \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} value comes from \texttt{erasePure\_\allowbreak{}erases}.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} a semantic predicate on the denotation of the mark, which is false for types (DV-32); verifying the oracle, which needs a typing metatheory for Lean; certificates on the closed mark alone, which cannot type a mark that mentions its enclosing binders; certifying the value of every constant of the closure, theorems' and recognized \texttt{casesOn}s' included, which the oracle has no marking of when a theorem's proof cites a constant outside the closure (every program with a nested proof, such as a \texttt{Fin} literal or \texttt{decide} on \texttt{Nat}) or a mutual \texttt{casesOn}'s value mentions \texttt{PUnit}, so that \texttt{hcert} is false on such programs; certifying only the values whose bodies the emitted environment holds, which the induction over the traversal can read only with a bound on the final environment threaded through every step and a proof that each traversal function keeps the registered constants; proving that the traversal's run on a value gives it a marking (the core lemma of \texttt{markOf\_\allowbreak{}exists\_\allowbreak{}statement}), which needs an invariant of every traversal function that the theorem does not otherwise use.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-38}{DV-38}}\label{reg:dv-38}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Spec.lean}: \leandecl{EraseProof.ConLecheAccepts}, hypothesis \texttt{hacc} of \leandecl{EraseProof.erase_correct_statement}, and \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Bridge/\allowbreak{}CLAccept.lean}, \leandecl{EraseProof.ConLecheAccepts.accepted}.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} \texttt{wf\_\allowbreak{}ext} (\texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICTyping.v:507}), the well-formedness of the global environment that \texttt{erase\_\allowbreak{}correct} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ErasureFunctionProperties.v:657}) takes as a hypothesis.
\item \textbf{What differs:} acceptance is con-leche's pure fold \leandecl{ConLeche.checkDeclsPure} at \leandecl{ConLeche.fueledOps} with the checker's fuel, with the empty \texttt{Nat.div}/\texttt{Nat.mod} pin list (CL ConLeche/MainTheorem.lean:70), on the declarations \leandecl{EraseProof.DeclsOf?} builds from the program, starting from the empty environment (CL ConLeche/Kernel/CheckDecl.lean:180): \texttt{P} contains in dependency order everything its records use, and the basis declarations in \texttt{P} are checked against con-leche's pins. The binary runs a different fold, \texttt{Cached.checkDecls} at the committed pin variants (\texttt{ConLeche.natOpPinSets}) and a Nat-size bound, on lean4export's output (CL ConLeche/MainTheorem.lean:102 model\_exists); the two are compared on the test programs and on Lean's \texttt{Eq}, \texttt{Quot} and \texttt{Nat} only. A program that declares \texttt{Nat.div} or \texttt{Nat.mod} is declined by the pure fold at the empty list. What acceptance gives is con-leche's own: the environment is well formed, has a model in every set theory, and its claims hold in every model (\leandecl{EraseProof.ConLecheAccepts.accepted}). Acceptance also requires \leandecl{EraseProof.RulesCanonical}: every stored recursor rule has the shape con-leche's generator writes (CL ConLeche/Kernel/Inductives/GenRec.lean:189 \texttt{classGenRule}, stored by \texttt{classRuleOk}, :444). con-leche proves that syntax at install only (CL ConLeche/Model/Inductives/GenRuleSyn.lean:292) and states of the accepted environment's rules their scoping and \texttt{\ensuremath{\lambda}}-count (CL ConLeche/Verify/EnvWF.lean:217); it is true of every accepted environment, is decidable, and is not derived from the fold here. \texttt{RulesCanonical} also requires that the rules of each recursor \texttt{T.rec} select by constructor (one rule per constructor of \texttt{T}, in order, each headed by its own constructor's minor premise, with that constructor's field count and as many arguments as the minor premise has binders, \leandecl{EraseProof.RulesSelected}) and that its K flag is the one con-leche's block check expects (CL ConLeche/Kernel/Inductives/RecCheck.lean:463 recKExpected), which con-leche checks at install and does not state of the accepted environment. It also requires that every recursor's level parameters be distinct (CL ConLeche/Kernel/CheckerBase.lean:112, checked at install and not stated of the accepted environment) and that every inductive hypothesis of a rule be a call of the recursor \texttt{t.rec} of a member \texttt{t} of the block (the recursor itself for a one-member block) at the recursor's own level parameters, with as many arguments as that recursor's major premise position plus one, under as many \texttt{\ensuremath{\lambda}}s as the minor premise's binder at its position has leading \texttt{\ensuremath{\Pi}}s, on the fields that the binders of the constructor's minor premise name, in order (\leandecl{EraseProof.IHShape}, \leandecl{EraseProof.RuleSelects}; the generator's callee \texttt{rec\_\allowbreak{}t}, CL ConLeche/Kernel/Inductives/GenRec.lean:189 \texttt{classGenRule}). It also requires that every rule of a recursor \texttt{T.rec} of a stored family fire \texttt{.plain} (CL ConLeche/Kernel/Env.lean:118 \texttt{RecRuleFire}, the installer's mode at a member major; the other modes are for auxiliary and quotient recursors) and that every stored definition's level parameters be distinct (CL ConLeche/Kernel/CheckerBase.lean:112, checked at install and not stated of the accepted environment). Acceptance also requires \leandecl{EraseProof.TablesCanonical}: every stored projection table names its structure's single constructor, at that constructor's parameter and field counts and level parameters; con-leche installs a table only from a structure's constructor but states of a stored table only its lookup (CL ConLeche/Verify/EnvWF.lean:22 Env.findProj?\_some). Acceptance also rejects a program whose declarations include an unsafe inductive: con-leche skips an unsafe block, so its constructors and recursors would be unchecked. It also rejects a program with a nested inductive (\texttt{numNested \ensuremath{\ne} 0}, \leandecl{EraseProof.blockShapeOK}): nested occurrences are outside the fragment (the simulation has no source \ensuremath{\iota} for their recursors), and for a non-nested block the records' recursors name members of the block, which the closure's reads use. It also requires that every recursor's type names every member of its block (\leandecl{EraseProof.blockShapeOK}): the fragment test reads a recursor's block only through its type, and con-leche compares the type with the generated one up to definitional equality, so a type that reaches a member only through a definition would pass. And it requires that every recursor's minor premises be syntactic domains of its type without \texttt{mdata}: the traversal counts a minor premise's binders with \leandecl{Erasure.minorArity}, which stops at \texttt{mdata}, while con-leche's reading \leandecl{EraseProof.toCL?} drops it.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} the main theorem of con-leche is stated for every pin list, so the empty list needs no pin data, which comes from con-leche's pin generator and is outside the hygiene allow list of check C6; the binary's driver is IO code (check C6) and the cached fold reads a lean4export stream, not Lean records, so neither is a function of the program's records. \texttt{RulesCanonical} and \texttt{TablesCanonical} are forced because con-leche states nothing about the stored rules' and tables' syntax beyond what its laws need (their scoping and \texttt{\ensuremath{\lambda}}-count, CL ConLeche/Verify/EnvWF.lean:217, and the lookup of a projection table, CL ConLeche/Verify/EnvWF.lean:22 Env.findProj?\_some): the shapes the traversal and the bridge read are checked at install and not stated of the accepted environment, so this reading checks them.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} the binary's fold at \texttt{natOpPinSets}, which needs the generated pin data and a stream; acceptance defined by con-leche's frontend on an export of the program, which is not a function of the records; \texttt{RulesCanonical} and \texttt{TablesCanonical} derived from the fold's block and structure installers instead of read from the program.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-39}{DV-39}}\label{reg:dv-39}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Spec.lean}: \leandecl{EraseProof.NoMarkKeys}, the hypothesis \texttt{hclean} of \leandecl{EraseProof.erase_correct_statement} (also in \leandecl{EraseProof.srcEval_sound_statement} and \leandecl{EraseProof.markOf_exists_statement}; its closure form \leandecl{EraseProof.NoMarkKeysDecls} is a premise of \leandecl{EraseProof.srcEval_sound_statement} and \leandecl{EraseProof.erase_correct_firstorder_statement}) and a condition of \leandecl{EraseProof.DeclsOf?}.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} none: PCUIC terms carry no metadata, so MetaRocq's erasure has nothing that could be mistaken for a mark.
\item \textbf{What differs:} the input and the types and values of the program carry no \texttt{mdata} node whose key is the anonymous name, the key of the marks (\leandecl{EraseProof.markMD}). Elaboration never writes such a key.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} a mark is an \texttt{mdata} node (Lean's \texttt{Expr} has no other carrier that the reading \texttt{toCL?} ignores, DV-1), and \texttt{unmark} removes the marks; an input node with the same key would be read as a mark, and \texttt{Sound} would compare the value with a term from which that node was removed.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} marks on a separate syntax, which duplicates every operation on \texttt{Expr} that the traversal, the source semantics and the bridge use; an \texttt{mdata} key chosen per program, which makes \texttt{MarkOf} depend on the key.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-40}{DV-40}}\label{reg:dv-40}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Test/\allowbreak{}NV1Premises.lean}, \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Test/\allowbreak{}NV2Premises.lean}, \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Test/\allowbreak{}NV3Premises.lean}, \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Test/\allowbreak{}NV4Premises.lean} and \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Test/\allowbreak{}NV5Premises.lean}: \leandecl{EraseProof.Test.NV1.hacc} to \leandecl{EraseProof.Test.NV5.hacc} take the fold equation \leandecl{ConLeche.checkDeclsPure}\texttt{ \ldots{} = .ok env} as a premise, and a \texttt{\#guard} in each file checks it by compiled evaluation (\texttt{EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Test/\allowbreak{}NV0Premises.lean} proves it in the kernel: NV-0 has no inductive type). In NV-3 and NV-4, \texttt{hty}, \texttt{hcert} and \texttt{hev} also take the premise \texttt{hg}: con-leche infers a type for the terms of \leandecl{EraseProof.Test.NV3.guardTerms} (NV-3), and the runs of \leandecl{EraseProof.Test.NV4.guards} succeed (NV-4); a \texttt{\#guard} checks each by compiled evaluation.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} \texttt{erase\_\allowbreak{}correct} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ErasureFunctionProperties.v:657}), whose hypotheses (\texttt{wf\_\allowbreak{}ext} among them, \texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICTyping.v:507}) have no non-vacuity requirement: MetaRocq does not exhibit a program that satisfies them.
\item \textbf{What differs:} the non-vacuity instances of \leandecl{EraseProof.erase_correct_statement} discharge every hypothesis in the kernel for NV-0. For a program with an inductive type (NV-1, NV-2, NV-5) the hypothesis \texttt{hacc} is discharged in the kernel except the one equation that con-leche's fold accepts the declarations and returns the stated environment; that equation is the premise of the theorem \texttt{hacc}, and the build fails if the compiled \texttt{\#guard} finds it false. In NV-3 and NV-4 the con-leche runs of \texttt{hty}, \texttt{hcert} and \texttt{hev} that compare a \ensuremath{\lambda} with the \texttt{\ensuremath{\Pi}} it fills, where the two bodies differ (a minor premise of \texttt{Nat.rec}, \texttt{Nat.casesOn} or \texttt{P.casesOn} against its \texttt{motive} applied, the proof \texttt{fun a b h =\textgreater{} h} of \texttt{Quot.lift}, and the proof of \texttt{P} built with \texttt{False.rec}), are premises in the same way; every other run of these instances is proved in the kernel, among them the \ensuremath{\iota} certificates of \texttt{recIota}, \texttt{casesLitZero}, \texttt{casesLitSucc} and the zero-field \texttt{casesFrozen} (\leandecl{EraseProof.IotaNoCertAt}) and of \texttt{quotLift} (\texttt{iotaCaseAt}). The instances are therefore conditional on computed, not kernel-checked, facts. MetaRocq counterpart: none.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} the kernel cannot reduce the fold on an inductive block. The block installer keeps its tables in \texttt{Std.HashMap}s (CL ConLeche/Kernel/FEnv.lean:36 FBase) hashed by Lean's \texttt{mixHash} (CL ConLeche/Kernel/Expr.lean:49 hashData), which is opaque to the kernel; and the checks that follow call the well-founded instantiateList (CL ConLeche/Kernel/ExprOps.lean:551 instantiateList) and leqCore (CL ConLeche/Kernel/Level.lean:87 leqCore), which the kernel does not unfold to a value; so does con-leche's binder congruence on two \texttt{\ensuremath{\Pi}}s that are not syntactically equal, which opens both bodies with instantiateList (CL ConLeche/Kernel/Core.lean:1478 defeqBinders). A program without an inductive type reduces to the end, which is why NV-0 needs no premise. The compiled \texttt{\#guard}s run con-leche's own compiled code, including its \texttt{implemented\_\allowbreak{}by} and \texttt{@[extern]} definitions (CL ConLeche/Kernel/Exclusive.lean:107, CL ConLeche/Kernel/NatHash.lean:54, its native \texttt{nat\_\allowbreak{}hash}), which is trusted for those checks only, not for the theorem.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} \texttt{native\_\allowbreak{}decide} or \texttt{ofReduceBool}, which adds the compiler to the trust base and is forbidden; a symbolic proof that the fold accepts the block, which needs the installer's \texttt{Std.HashMap} reasoning and every comparison above proved by hand; kernel-reducible twins of these functions in con-leche, which the verification does not add (it never extends con-leche); restricting the non-vacuity programs to those without inductive types, which leaves every rule about \texttt{casesOn}, constructors and \ensuremath{\eta}-expanded constructors without an instance.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{DV-41}{DV-41}}\label{reg:dv-41}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Our artifact:} \leanfile{proof/\allowbreak{}EraseProof/\allowbreak{}Statements.lean}: the hypothesis \texttt{hev} of \leandecl{EraseProof.erase_correct_statement} and of \leandecl{EraseProof.erase_correct_firstorder_statement}, and the evaluation premise of \leandecl{EraseProof.srcEval_sound_statement}: \leandecl{EraseProof.SrcEval} in \leandecl{EraseProof.evalEnvOf}\texttt{ view cfg decls}, over the closure \texttt{decls} the fragment test returns; the erasure relation of the conclusions of \leandecl{EraseProof.erase_correct_statement} and the first-order value of \leandecl{EraseProof.erase_correct_firstorder_statement} over the same environment.
\item \textbf{Reference artifact:} MetaRocq's \texttt{erase\_\allowbreak{}correct} (\texttt{erasure/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}ErasureFunctionProperties.v:657}), whose source evaluation \texttt{eval} (\texttt{pcuic/\allowbreak{}theories/\allowbreak{}PCUICWcbvEval.v:230}; MC \S{}5.6) is in the global environment \texttt{\ensuremath{\Sigma}}.
\item \textbf{What differs:} the source semantics is the program's evaluation in its dependency closure as \texttt{\#erase} computes it (\leandecl{Erasure.collectDeps}): \ensuremath{\delta} unfolds, and the \texttt{casesOn}, constructor, recursor and projection rules look up, only declarations of the closure, and \ensuremath{\delta} marks an unfolded value with \leandecl{EraseProof.MarkOf} over the closure. The closure is a sub-environment of the program (\leandecl{EraseProof.collectDeps_sub}), so con-leche's acceptance of the program and its models apply to every declaration the evaluation reads. The erasure relation of the conclusion reads the same declarations, and each \ensuremath{\lambda}\ensuremath{\Box} body erases the markings of its value over the closure (\texttt{ErasesDecl}). MetaRocq evaluates in the whole global environment.
\item \textbf{Why it is forced:} the marks are the eraser's oracle's decisions (\leandecl{Erasure.Pure.isErasable}), which it takes over the closure, and its reductions unfold the definitions of the list it reads; the closure does not read the value of a recognized \texttt{casesOn}, whose constants may lie outside it (a mutual \texttt{casesOn}'s value mentions \texttt{PUnit}), so the marking over the program can differ from the marking over the closure, and \ensuremath{\delta} over the program would mark unfolded values with decisions the eraser does not take.
\item \textbf{What was considered instead:} evaluation over the program with a theorem that the marking over the closure is the marking over the program on the expressions the traversal reads, which needs an agreement theory of the oracle between two declaration lists and an invariant for the \texttt{casesOn} values the closure does not read (about 2500 to 2900 lines); a change of the shipping closure so that it reads those values, which still needs the agreement theory (about 1300 lines).
\end{itemize}
